event: The last Nala remembers is her back window: a book on her knee, the evening going blue.

memory.fact: The last thing Alan remembers is dozing over a book at his back window one evening.

event: Then cold wet grass against her cheek, a smell of earth and old smoke, and she opens her eyes.

memory.fact: Nala woke inside the Waystone Shrine's ring at dawn on day one.

event: Grey stones, lichen-spotted and taller than a man, stand in a ring round her under a pale sky.

memory.fact: The ring's standing stones are grey and lichen-spotted, each taller than a man.
The shrine is a roofless ring of standing stones on a grassy hilltop beside a hill road.

event: She pushes herself up, and her arms are wrong: thin, the hands small, pale and freckled.

memory.fact: Her hands are small and pale, with a few freckles across the backs, and her feet are small.

event: Her hands do what she tells them a half second late, as if still learning how.

memory.fact: Her new body answers her a half second late, as if still learning how.

event: Long, heavy, dark red hair falls across her face and runs on past her shoulder blades.

memory.fact: Her hair is long, heavy and dark red, falling past her shoulder blades.

event: Her old grey shirt hangs off her to mid-thigh; her black tights are soaked through at the knees.

memory.fact: She wears Alan's loose dark grey shirt, which hangs to her mid-thigh and gapes at the collar.
She wears Alan's black compression tights, which still fit her snugly.

event: Her feet are bare and small. Her chest is not her chest; she looks once, then at the stones.
She gets up, and the ground is lower than it should be.

memory.fact: Her body looks about twenty-five, petite, and a head shorter than Alan was.

event: At the ring's centre sits a waist-high grey altar stone, carved with a door and a key.

memory.fact: At the ring's centre is a flat grey altar stone, carved with a door and a key.

event: On it lie offerings: a green copper coin, a dried flower, a crust with tooth marks in it.

memory.fact: Travellers leave small offerings on the altar: a copper coin, a dried flower, a bread crust.

event: Outside the ring a two-rut road curls down into a misty valley, where roofs and smoke show.

memory.fact: The hill road winds down the slope to a river valley, where a village's roofs show.
It is early morning; dew is on the grass and mist lies in the valley below.

event: Birds start below; her breath shows, and her bare feet go numb in the wet grass.
The coin on the altar catches the first light, and she sets off toward the roofs.
Just outside the gap a ninth stone lies fallen outward, half sunk in the grass.

memory.fact: The ring has nine stones; one has fallen outward and lies in the grass.

event: The road's ruts are full of sharp stones, so she walks the grass strip down the middle.

memory.fact: A hill road of two ruts runs over the ridges between the scattered farms and villages.

event: Downhill her stride comes out short; twice she pitches forward and catches herself late.
Juniper and gorse crowd the slope, and thyme crushes sharp-smelling under her bare feet.

memory.fact: Juniper and gorse crowd the slope below the ring, and thyme grows in the road's grass strip.

event: The mist thins: more flat roofs come out of it, and more threads of hearth smoke.
Her feet ache with cold deep in the bones, and the wet tights chill her knees at every step.
Past a bend below, sheep bells knock, and a dog starts barking, hard and fast.
A shaggy grey dog rounds the bend and plants itself in the road, hackles up, barking at her.

memory.fact: Smoke barks at strangers on the road until Tobin or Wenna calls her off.

event: Sheep and goats follow, bells clanking, and behind them a lanky boy of fifteen with a crook.
He sees her and stops dead; his free hand goes to the sling looped at his belt.
The sun clears the eastern ridge, and light runs down the road and lies between them.

memory.fact: At sunrise on day one Nala met a shepherd boy, his flock and his grey dog Smoke on the hill road.

event: "Smoke! Down," he snaps. The dog drops flat in the road, still growling low.
His eyes go to her bare feet and black-tighted legs; he goes red, and keeps to her face.

memory.fact: Tobin would stare at a barefoot red-haired woman, blush, and then ask a hundred questions.
A woman in a man's shirt with her legs' shape showing would shock Tavelford.
Nala came down from the Old Waystone barefoot, in tights, with her red hair loose.

event: He glances up at the ring and back. "Sardanal keep you," he says, and stays well back.

memory.fact: Hill folk greet a stranger with 'Sardanal keep you' and wait to be told the stranger's business.

event: His words are in no language she has heard, yet she understands them as plainly as English.

memory.fact: Nala understands the local speech as plainly as English, though it is no tongue she knows.

event: "Excuse me, sir. What are those stones behind me?" It comes out in his language, easily.

memory.fact: Nala speaks the local speech as easily as English, though she never learned it.

event: He grins at the "sir", a front tooth chipped: he is Tobin Ashlar, and he doesn't get sirred.

changes.note: Nala meets Tobin on the hill road, and a bond with him starts at nothing

memory.fact: The shepherd boy on the hill road is named Tobin Ashlar.
Tobin's voice cracks, and he asks questions without waiting for the answers.

event: His hand leaves the sling. He is sunburnt, black-curled, in a sheepskin worn wool side in.

memory.fact: Tobin is sunburnt, with a mop of black curls and a chipped front tooth.
Tobin wears a sheepskin cloak, wool side in, and carries a sling.

event: "That's the Old Waystone. Maradoc's ring. Don't you have waystones where you're from?"

memory.fact: The Old Waystone is also called Maradoc's ring.

event: Travellers stop there for a safe road, he says, and touch the key on the altar.

memory.fact: Travellers stop at the ring for a safe road and touch the key on the altar.

event: Who raised it is anyone's guess; Mam says Maradoc did, and it's older than the Old Empire.

memory.fact: Hill folk call the ring the Old Waystone; no one in the valley knows who raised it.
Hill tales say the waystones are older than the Old Empire and were raised by Maradoc.
Tobin has a mother, whom he calls Mam.

event: The one lying down fell in a storm when his grandfather was little.

memory.fact: The fallen stone fell in a storm when Tobin's grandfather was little.

event: It hums sometimes on still nights; Smoke won't go inside, and the dogs all stop at the stones.

memory.fact: Shepherds say the ring hums on still nights, and their dogs will not go inside it.

event: Blushing again, he keeps on: did she sleep up there, for Maradoc's keeping? Where are her shoes?

memory.fact: Travellers on the hill road sometimes sleep inside the ring for Maradoc's keeping.

event: Was she robbed? By the soldiers from the old tower? Is she from Param?

memory.fact: Tobin knows of soldiers at the old tower, and fears they rob travellers.

event: The dog creeps forward on her belly and sniffs at Nala's bare toes.

memory.fact: Smoke would circle a barefoot stranger, sniff her feet, and then lean on her legs.

event: Nala asks if the Old Empire is the one overrun by the dead, and where, precisely, she is.
"Harrak? You know about Harrak?" It's over the sea in Param; the dead took it long ago.

memory.fact: To Tobin the Old Empire is Harrak, over the sea in Param, which fell to the dead long ago.

event: Joss the carter says a witch-queen rules the dead lands now; he hears things in Imra.

memory.fact: Tobin has heard from Joss's news that a witch-queen now rules Harrak's dead lands.
Joss is a carter who hears news in Imra.

event: He points his crook at her, pleased: "So you are from Param. I knew it."

memory.fact: Tobin takes Nala for Paramese.
Tobin would guess any strange stranger is Paramese, since he has never seen an outlander.
Most Tavelford folk have never seen an outlander, and take strange strangers for Paramese.

event: This is the Tavel valley in Asmirel, he says: Prince Tavaris's land, may Sardanal bless him.

memory.fact: Asmirel is Prince Tavaris's land, and the Tavel valley lies in it.
Viziman lords are styled with "may Sardanal bless him".

event: Tavelford's down there where the smoke is; Imra is two days on, down the river.

memory.fact: Tavelford lies in the valley below the waystone ring, where the hearth smoke rises.
Imra is two days down the river from Tavelford.
Tobin names his home as the Tavel valley in Asmirel, Prince Tavaris's land, two days above Imra.

event: Then the rest of what she said catches up with him, and the grin goes.
"Waystones don't take anybody anywhere. They're shrines." He sounds less sure than he did.

memory.fact: Tobin has never heard of a waystone carrying anyone; to him they are shrines, not roads.

event: The dog gives up on her toes and sits leaning against her shin, warm and heavy.
"Mam knows all the old tales. She'd know if..." He stops and chews his lip.

memory.fact: Tobin's mother knows all the old tales.

event: Their farm's the first house down the road; he has the flock till noon, but Mam's home.

memory.fact: Tobin keeps the flock on the hill till noon.

event: He points with the crook: far below, a stone house and a sheepfold come out of the mist.

memory.fact: The Ashlar farm, a stone house and a sheepfold, is the first house down the hill road.

event: Nala asks him to take her to talk to his Mam.
He's not meant to leave the flock, he says; then, fast: Smoke can hold them an hour, anyway.

memory.fact: Tobin may not leave the flock untended; Smoke can hold it on the hill for an hour or so.

event: He crouches by the dog: "Smoke. Keep them." Smoke trots off up the road to the flock.

memory.fact: Smoke keeps the Ashlar flock on her own when Tobin tells her to.

event: They go down the road together, Tobin walking an arm's length off to one side.
He talks the whole way: whose terrace is whose, which ridge the scalehounds come down in spring.

memory.fact: Scalehounds come down off a ridge above the Tavel valley in spring.

event: He asks things and answers them himself: "You've got sheep in Param? You must. Everyone does."
Lower down the grass strip thins; the road stones bite her soles, and her feet begin to throb.
The sun climbs, and the wet knees of her tights start to steam.
Barefoot she is slow; near an hour on, they reach a low stone house with a blue door.

memory.fact: The Ashlar farmhouse is low and stone, with a blue door.
The Ashlar farm is the better part of an hour's barefoot walk down the road from the ring.
The Ashlar farm is the better part of an hour's barefoot walk down the road from the ring.

event: Along the yard wall, a pen of hurdles is loud with ewes and new lambs.

memory.fact: A hurdle lambing pen runs along the yard wall, loud with ewes and new lambs.

event: Two small girls feeding hens in the yard stop dead and stare at her, mouths open.

memory.fact: Two small girls feed the hens in the Ashlar yard.

event: The blue door opens on a tall, rawboned woman with a stick, grey threading her dark hair.

changes.note: Nala comes to Wenna's door, and a bond with her starts at nothing

memory.fact: Tobin's Mam is tall and rawboned, with grey threading her dark hair.
Tobin's Mam met Nala at her door with a stick in her hand.
Tobin's Mam met Nala at her door with a stick in her hand.

event: She wears a faded red robe and a brown headcloth.

memory.fact: Tobin's Mam wears a faded red robe and a brown headcloth.

event: Tobin blurts that she came down from the Old Waystone, that she's from Param and knows Harrak.

memory.fact: Tobin takes Nala for Paramese.
Nala came down from the Old Waystone barefoot, in tights, with her red hair loose.

event: The woman looks at her bare feet, the tights, the loose red hair, and her mouth goes flat.

memory.fact: Tavelford women cover their hair outdoors and wear long skirts or robes to the ankle.

event: She glances up the hill toward the ring, and her hand tightens on the stick.

memory.fact: Wenna would take a barefoot stranger come down from the ring for a stray, and be uneasy.
Wenna would meet a stranger in the yard with a stick, then soften if the stranger worked.

event: Without a word she goes in, and comes out holding a folded brown headcloth out to Nala.

memory.fact: Tobin's Mam held out a spare brown headcloth to Nala without a word.
Tobin's Mam held out a spare brown headcloth to Nala without a word.
Wenna would hand an uncovered stranger woman her own spare headcloth without a word.

event: Then, flat, to her son: "Tobin. The flock." He goes red and stays where he is.

memory.fact: Tobin's Mam told him to go back to the flock; he flushed and stayed.

event: The woman turns her eyes on Nala: "What do you want at my door?"
Nala begs pardon for pulling her boy off, and asks for tales of travellers come by no road.

memory.fact: Nala asked Wenna for tales of travellers who come to waystones by no road.
Nala asked Wenna for tales of travellers who come to waystones by no road.

event: "He pulled himself. Flock. Now." Tobin jogs back up the road, looking over his shoulder twice.

memory.fact: Wenna sent Tobin back to the flock, and this time he went, looking back twice.

event: She lays the headcloth over Nala's hair herself and tugs it straight with two hard fingers.

memory.fact: Wenna laid her spare headcloth over Nala's hair herself and tugged it straight at the brow.

event: The two girls creep up behind her, hens forgotten, staring at the red hair under the cloth.
"There are tales. My grandmother's." A stray steps out of a waystone at dawn, no road dust.

memory.fact: Hill tale: a stray steps out of a waystone at dawn with no road dust on her feet.
Grandmothers' tales tell of Maradoc's strays: lost folk found at waystones far from home.

event: Her eyes drop to Nala's feet, grey now with the road's dust, and come back up.

memory.fact: Nala's bare feet are grey with the hill road's dust.
Nala's bare feet are grey with the hill road's dust.

event: "They speak the tongue of wherever they land. Never learned it."

memory.fact: Hill tale: strays speak the tongue of the land they come to, though they never learned it.

event: One came at a waystone near Imra long ago: a man who stayed a year, mended the mill, and left.

memory.fact: Hill tale: a stray came to a waystone near Imra some five generations back.
In that tale the Imra stray, a man, stayed a year, mended the mill, and walked off one dawn.

event: "Maradoc doesn't waste a stray, Gran used to say. He sets each one where there's work."

memory.fact: Hill saying: Maradoc does not waste a stray; he sets each where some work wants doing.

event: For a moment her eyes go to the lambing pen along the wall, loud with ewes.
"The wayfarer priest comes through each spring. Soon. He'd know more than me."

memory.fact: Wenna knows the Maradoc wayfarer priest comes each spring, soon, and would know more.
A Maradoc wayfarer priest walks the hill waystones each spring and lodges in Tavelford.

event: She leans on the stick: "Or it's a tale, and you're a runaway with a clever story. Which?"

memory.fact: Wenna asked Nala outright whether she is a stray or a runaway with a clever story.
Wenna half-believes the tales; she thinks a stray is as likely a runaway with a clever story.

event: A runaway would dress more practically, Nala says, and holds up her empty hands: no shoes.

memory.fact: She has no shoes, no money and nothing in her hands.

event: She was at home with a book, then in the waystones; pulled into the gods' schemes, she'll learn why.

memory.fact: Nala told Wenna she was at home with a book, then in the middle of the waystones.
Nala told Wenna she was pulled into the gods' schemes, and means to learn why.

event: "A book." Books are lords' things, priests' things; she can't read a word of one.

memory.fact: Wenna cannot read; to her a book is a lord's or a priest's thing.

event: She takes the grey shirt's hem between finger and thumb: good cloth, unpatched.

memory.fact: Nala's grey shirt is good cloth, unpatched.

event: "The gods are busy, and far off. They don't pluck women off hearths."

memory.fact: Wenna holds that the gods are busy and far off, and do not pluck women from hearths.

event: A ewe bleats long in the pen. Forty ewes lambing, she says, and not hands enough; no coin to pay.

memory.fact: Wenna needs another pair of hands for the lambing and cannot pay for one in coin.

event: She pays in bread, a hearth bed and a roof, and a robe will keep the valley from staring.

memory.fact: Wenna could give a woman a robe, a bed by the hearth and meals for help with the lambing.

event: Leave the gods at her door: the wayfarer will judge her tale. Till then she's a woman off the hill.

memory.fact: Wenna would hold a tale of god-touched for the wayfarer priest to judge when he comes.

event: "Work first. Then I'll know what you are."

memory.fact: Wenna judges a stranger by work done, not by a tale told.

event: Nala will gladly work, but warns she has never touched a sheep: she'll need teaching.

changes.note: Nala takes the work and owns plainly she knows nothing of sheep (standing +2)

memory.fact: Nala had never touched a sheep before the Ashlar farm.

event: The woman looks at her a moment longer, then nods once, short, like a gate shutting.
She brings a faded red robe, ankle-length and thin at the elbows: put it over what she has.

memory.fact: Wenna gave Nala a faded red robe, ankle-length and thin at the elbows, to wear over her clothes.
Wenna's spare robe is faded madder red, ankle-length and far too large for Nala.

event: Nala pulls it on; the sleeves swallow her hands, and the hem drags on the yard stones.
From the woodpile, the older girl whispers, and the little one giggles.
"Your name?" "Nala," she says. The woman repeats it once, flat, weighing it.

memory.fact: Nala told Wenna her name.
Alan woke in a woman's body, and in this body she calls herself Nala.

event: To the girls: "Pell. Lissa. This is Nala. She works here now."

memory.fact: Wenna's daughters are named Pell and Lissa.
Wenna took Nala on to work the Ashlar farm and told her girls so.

event: She puts a wooden bucket in Nala's hands and points her at the rock cistern.

changes.note: Nala's first farm work, at Wenna's cistern, starts her Farmhand skill

make.title: Farmhand
make.description: The plain work of a hill steading: water, fodder, muck, fences and driving stock.

memory.fact: Water for the Ashlar yard is drawn from a rock cistern.

event: Water first, then fodder, then the pen: the day has a plain order, and it goes on and on.

memory.fact: Wenna sets a novice to water, fodder and muck first, and to the ewes only when trusted.

event: The yard stones press up through her soles at every step, and the bucket handle bites.
Wenna teaches as they go: move slow, come at a ewe from the side, never grab the wool.

changes.note: Wenna's first lessons in handling ewes start Nala's Lambing skill

make.title: Lambing
make.description: Attending a ewe at birth: catching the lamb, clearing its mouth and setting it to suck.

memory.fact: Wenna's way with ewes: move slow, come at a ewe from the side, never grab the wool.

event: The girls trail her everywhere with small buckets of their own, telling her which hens bite.

memory.fact: Pell and Lissa carry water and feed the hens, and would follow Nala everywhere.

event: They show her the pen: ewes, lambs, and one ewe lying apart with her head turned away.
Wenna goes still at the sight, and takes the bucket from Nala's hands without looking.
The ewe is down and does not get up; Wenna is over the hurdles and kneeling in the straw.
"One lamb," she says, hands in the fleece, feeling. "It's turned." She does not look up.

memory.fact: A ewe lies down in the Ashlar lambing pen and cannot rise; her one lamb is turned.

event: Straw is scattered where the ewe has dragged herself round and round the pen.
